headline: SSC and equivalent exam results published today; check online, SMS, or institutes
summary: The results for this year's SSC and equivalent examinations are being released today, August 10. Education Minister Dr. Anm Ehsanul Hoque Milan will inaugurate the results at 10 AM.
details: The wait for the results of this year's SSC and equivalent examinations concludes today, Monday, August 10. Education Minister Dr. Anm Ehsanul Hoque Milan will inaugurate the results at 10 AM in a ceremony at the Ministry of Education conference room.

Students can access their results simultaneously online, through their educational institutions, and via mobile SMS. This information was announced in a Ministry of Education notification on Sunday, August 9.

The chairmen of all education boards will hand over the exam results to the Education Minister during the inauguration. Professor Dr. Syed Akhtaruzzaman, Chairman of Dhaka Education Board and President of Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee, confirmed the simultaneous publication of results at 10 AM.

Results will be available on the respective education board websites. Additionally, two common websites, eduboardresult.gov.bd and educationboardresults.gov.bd, will also provide the results. Students can also collect their results directly from their educational institutions.

To get results via SMS, type 'SSC <Board_initials> <Roll_number> <Year>' and send to 16140. For example, 'SSC DHA 123456 2024' for Dhaka Board. A charge of BDT 1.39, including all taxes, applies per SMS.

A total of 1,857,344 students filled out forms for this year's SSC and equivalent examinations. This includes 1,418,398 for SSC under general boards, 304,286 for Dakhil under Madrasa Board, and 134,660 for SSC (Vocational) under Technical Board.
Applications for result re-scrutiny will be accepted online from August 11 to August 17. Detailed instructions for the application process will be published on the education boards' websites.

headline_marked: [[16 Bangladeshis die in Saudi sofa factory fire]]; Ministers express deep sorrow
headline: 16 Bangladeshis die in Saudi sofa factory fire; Ministers express deep sorrow
summary: Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam expressed profound grief and sympathy for the victims and their families. The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh is actively working to identify the deceased and complete f
details: Sixteen Bangladeshi expatriate workers tragically lost their lives in a devastating fire at a sofa manufacturing factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Sunday night.
Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam expressed deep sorrow and heartfelt condolences over the tragic loss of lives.
They conveyed profound sympathy to the bereaved families of the deceased Bangladeshi citizens and assured them of support during this irreparable loss and time of grief.

Upon receiving news of the incident, officials from the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh promptly arrived at the scene. The embassy is closely coordinating with Saudi authorities to identify the victims and complete necessary formalities for their repatriation.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is continuously monitoring the situation and providing assistance as required.
Reports indicate that ten of the deceased hailed from Naogaon district, and three were residents of Natore district in Bangladesh.
caption:
A devastating fire at a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has claimed the lives of 16 Bangladeshi expatriate workers.

Sixteen Bangladeshi expatriate workers tragically lost their lives in a devastating fire at a sofa manufacturing factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Sunday night.

Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam expressed deep sorrow and heartfelt condolences over the tragic loss of lives.

They conveyed profound sympathy to the bereaved families of the deceased Bangladeshi citizens and assured them of support during this irreparable loss and time of grief.

Upon receiving news of the incident, officials from the Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh promptly arrived at the scene. The embassy is closely coordinating with Saudi authorities to identify the victims and complete necessary formalities for their repatriation.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is continuously monitoring the situation and providing assistance as required.

Reports indicate that ten of the deceased hailed from Naogaon district, and three were residents of Natore district in Bangladesh.
